correctness.rationale: The lower bound follows because undirected adjacency is quantifier-free definable by \(S(x,y)\lor S(y,x)\), so Brown--Hoshino's exact undirected separating sentences transfer without increasing rank. For the upper bound, their cycle proof cuts at the first chosen vertex and invokes an endpoint-preserving path strategy; inspection of the primary proof shows that its coordinate responses preserve signed displacement and corresponding left/right endpoint gaps, hence preserve successor orientation as well as undirected adjacency. The q=1 and q=2 cases are checked directly. A fresh independent exact EF-game solver agreed with the formula on 144 cycle pairs over \(1\le q\le4\), \(3\le m\le n\le10\); this is corroboration only.

final_claim: For directed successor cycles \(\vec C_n\), Duplicator wins the \(q\)-round Ehrenfeucht--Fraisse game on \(\vec C_m,\vec C_n\) exactly when \(m=n\) or both lengths are at least \(g(q)\), where \(g(1)=1\), \(g(2)=4\), and \(g(q)=2^{q-1}+3\) for \(q\ge3\).
limitations: Single consistently oriented finite cycles only, in the successor-only relational language.
No counting logic, named vertices, arbitrary orientations, or disjoint unions are covered.
